objective: Pin the exact construction of the Jiang-Li-Wang signed high-frequency news-return feature from primary and corroborating sources before building it locally, and gather enough context (post-2012 replication status, related adaptations, data caveats) to judge whether the local build and its preregistered signal-card tests are worth the compute.
existing_solution_comparison: The mechanism (signed high-frequency price reaction to firm news, aggregated into a daily 'news return', predicting subsequent drift) is a peer-reviewed, published construction (JFE 2021), read here from the authors' own 2019 working-paper draft; it is mechanistically distinct from this project's already-refuted count/novelty-based news-attention family. No local prior attempt at this exact construction exists.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:news_attention_features (refuted 2026-09-16, count/novelty only); checked via `oc research directions check` before starting this iteration, no other direction constructs a signed HF news-reaction feature.

sources.core_claim: M=26 interval grid per day: 1 overnight (prior 4pm close to current 9:45am price) + 25 intraday 15-minute intervals (9:45am-4pm); TAQ prices split/dividend-adjusted via CRSP factors.
sources.project_applicability: Exact grid replicated on our 1-minute SIP bars in scripts/build_news_hf_reaction.py.
sources.reflection: Read by direct PDF page rendering (image-based), hand-transcribed since the fetch tool could not extract machine text from this specific PDF; cross-checked against Hao Jiang's CV and the crossref bibliographic record for the published version.

sources.core_claim: Regular-hours news -> same-interval 15-min return; weekend/holiday/overnight news -> nearest subsequent overnight return (worked example: weekend news gets Friday-4pm-to-Monday-9:45am).
sources.reflection: Same reading method as above; this rule is the single most load-bearing design choice in the local build and is quoted verbatim in direction-review.json.

sources.core_claim: Equal-weighted decile sort at 4pm close, one-week overlapping holding: decile1 -0.78%/mo to decile10 +2.55%/mo, spread 3.34%/mo (t=11.72), FFC4 alpha 3.37%/mo (t=11.76), 2000-2012.
sources.project_applicability: Headline magnitude and long-short structure motivating a long-only (direction +1) signal-card test.
sources.reflection: Gross of costs; no transaction-cost scenario found in this draft's readable sections -- the registry's ~18bp/~1.37%-net figure is not independently re-verified this pass.

sources.core_claim: Overnight news is more than half of the paper's full sample and shows delayed (not immediate) reaction once tested with an intraday event-study design.
sources.project_applicability: Corroborated locally: 57.1% of our own 2024+ news items arrive outside 09:30-16:00 ET (see data-feasibility.json), so the overnight bucket is not a minor edge case here either.
sources.reflection: Independent local measurement, not a re-run of the paper's own overnight event study.

sources.core_claim: SSRN DOI 10.2139/ssrn.2679614's abstract matches the Duke working-paper draft's abstract verbatim -- same paper.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms the working-paper draft and the JFE-published paper the registry cites are one and the same.
sources.reflection: Bibliographic/abstract match only; SSRN and ScienceDirect both returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch this pass, so the full published text was not independently read.

sources.core_claim: Hao Jiang's own CV lists 'Jiang, Hao, Sophia Li and Hao Wang (2021). Pervasive Underreaction: Evidence from High-Frequency Data. Journal of Financial Economics 141: 573-599', winner of Best Paper Awards at the Eleventh Triple Crown Conference.
sources.project_applicability: Independently confirms the working-paper draft's later publication venue, volume/page numbers, and that it is peer-reviewed (not just a permanent working paper).
sources.reflection: This specific PDF turned out to be Hao Jiang's CV, not the paper itself, when first fetched while searching for a free full-text copy -- kept as a source because the CV's own publication-list line is independently useful bibliographic confirmation.

sources.core_claim: Journal of Financial Economics's own page lists this article under the title 'Pervasive underreaction: Evidence from high-frequency data', confirming the DOI family and journal placement found by search.
sources.project_applicability: Corroborates the paper's existence and journal placement; contributes no additional methodology detail (fetch returned HTTP 403, abstract-only page not retrievable this pass).
sources.reflection: Could not be fetched (403); listed here only because it was one of the first and most consistently returned search results across every query this pass, and its non-retrievability is itself a disclosed limitation.

sources.core_claim: "Dissecting Momentum in China" (Liu, Tan, Xu, Yuan, Zhu, April 2026) explicitly builds on Jiang et al. (2021)'s news/non-news decomposition ('This method is inspired by Jiang et al. (2021), who decomposed daily stock returns into news-driven and non-news-driven components') but classifies whole DAYS (not 15-minute intervals) as news/non-news and sorts on the past 5-day news return at MONTHLY rebalance on Chinese equities; the resulting quintile long-short spread is not significant (0.10%/month, t=0.31), i.e. this coarser day-level, different-market, different-horizon adaptation does not reproduce a positive result.
sources.project_applicability: The only post-2012, non-registry evidence found this pass that engages with the JLW construction directly; a genuine caution (not a refutation, given the methodological differences) about assuming the effect transfers easily outside the original HF/US/weekly design -- directly relevant to this iteration's own remaining_evidence_gap.
sources.reflection: Read via pdftotext extraction (this PDF's text layer was machine-readable, unlike the Duke PDF); the null result is for a DAY-level decomposition and MONTHLY horizon in CHINA, not the 15-minute/US/weekly construction this iteration actually builds, so it is evidence about adaptation risk, not a like-for-like replication failure.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: The paper's own grid starts intraday intervals at 9:45am, folding the 9:30-9:45 opening-auction window into the overnight interval by construction, not as an approximation.
candidate_matrix_revisions.revision: attribute_news() classifies any news before a session's own 9:45 anchor as overnight for that session, not as a same-day intraday bucket -- an exact rule, not a simplification

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: Overnight news is more than half the sample in both the paper's data and ours (57.1% locally).
candidate_matrix_revisions.revision: kept the full overnight-interval machinery (chained prior-session close to next-session 9:45 anchor) rather than dropping or approximating overnight news as a simplification for build speed

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: A coarser day-level, monthly-horizon, different-market adaptation of the same decomposition did not find a significant effect.
candidate_matrix_revisions.revision: kept the paper's own fine-grained 15-minute/weekly construction (not a day-level shortcut) precisely so this build is not exposed to the same failure mode; flagged as an open risk in direction-review.json rather than treated as resolved
